entries.defect: Prerequisites and evidence stance. Steps 1-2 of the amendment (global Codex CLI 0.163.0, probe `codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol` OK on 20.10.2026 08:10) are accepted from the owner record; the implementer does not repeat the install. If the global probe fails in the implementing session, stop and report before any rename. The inventory is grep evidence, not inspected source: every count and excerpt (I12 en.ts is cut mid-line) is confirmed in the tree during implementation, not assumed. Half A's entries arrived truncated after their first line, so where A's reasoning could not be read the decision below rests on B's text and the spec.

The registry: a frozen `LANES` array of three records with stable role keys `main`, `cross`, `scarce` (DECIDED: both halves use these names; nothing is called 'alternate'). Fields: role, vendor (token from the VENDORS table), displayName, trailerName (the long form used in trailers, e.g. `Claude Opus 5.5`), modelId, retired (array of name/id spellings, U6), runtime (`claude`|`codex`), scarce (boolean), reasoningEffort (replaces ASTRA_REASONING_EFFORT; no env override is added because none is proven to exist). Initial data: main = Claude Opus 5.5 / claude-opus-5-5[1m] / claude; scarce = Fable 5.1 / claude-fable-5-1 / claude / scarce:true; cross = GPT-6.1 Sol / gpt-6.1-sol / codex, display name marked in a comment as the user's assumption. Vendor and runtime are separate fields; runtime is never used as a vendor proxy.

Fallback and history stay flat fields. The main record carries `fallbackModelId` / `fallbackDisplayName` (Opus 4.8 / claude-opus-4-8[1m]) so the existing refusal fallback keeps working without Opus 4.8 becoming a lane; retired spellings are recognition-only and never executable. REJECTED B5/B6 (identity descriptors plus a selected-identity key with derived current fields): a one-line switch is already achieved by editing modelId/displayName and appending the old names to `retired`; the descriptor layer is a new abstraction the infrastructure freeze does not justify.

`VENDORS` table in the same module: `{ anthropic: { trailerAddress: 'noreply@anthropic.com' }, openai: { trailerAddress: 'noreply@openai.com' } }` plus any legacy address forms landed trailers use. model-guard-core derives what today is `ALLOWED` (regex `astra|sol`), `FABLE_ALLOWED`, `MODEL_FAMILY_WORD` and `MODEL_VENDOR_ADDRESS` from LANES/VENDORS at import time; `isOpenAiLane` is deleted, callers compare `lane.vendor`. No consumer file contains a vendor name or email domain.

Retired names per lane, from the measured history: cross = GPT-6 Astra, gpt-6-astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, gpt-5.6-sol; main = Opus 5, Claude Opus 5, claude-opus-5[1m], claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-20260801 (plus the '(1M context)' suffix handled by the parser grammar, U9); scarce = Fable 5, Claude Fable 5, claude-fable-5, Claude Fable 5.1. Haiku, Sonnet, Nano, GPT-7 Astra and gpt-does-not-exist are NOT registered: the inventory shows them only in negative tests. DECIDED: current and retired names collapse to their lane for EVERY lane, not only for cross; the rule is one generic data lookup, and the spec's 'all three as one lane' is the cross instance of it. `resolveModel` returns the lane and the matched spelling so historical attribution is preserved while identity is unified.

Pure exported helpers, no filesystem, subprocess, env or probe at import: `lane(role)` throws on unknown role; `lanes()`; `resolveModel(value)` returns `{lane, matched}` or null, never defaults to main; `sameLane(a, b)`; `differentVendor(a, b)`; `eligibleReviewers(authorLanes)`; `trailerFor(role, {fallback})` (U17). Every helper takes an optional `registry` argument defaulting to LANES so tests can pass synthetic registries. B17 partly REJECTED: `identityForExecution(role, selection)` belongs to the rejected selection layer (U3); execution reads `lane(role).modelId` or the main fallback field directly. `formatTrailer` is folded into `trailerFor`.

No role-renamed constant copies. ASTRA_MODEL, ASTRA_MODEL_ID, ASTRA_MODEL_NAME, ASTRA_TRAILER, FABLE_MODEL, FABLE_MODEL_ID, FABLE_TRAILER, OPUS_MODEL, OPUS_MODEL_ID, OPUS_FALLBACK_MODEL(_ID), CLAUDE_MODEL are deleted; consumers read `lane('cross').modelId`, `trailerFor('scarce')`, `lane('main').fallbackModelId`. The only role-named constants exported are the three records themselves (`MAIN`, `CROSS`, `SCARCE`) for the handful of consumers that prefer a static import.

Registry invariants are asserted by the registry's own unit test, not by runtime validation (freeze): unique roles, every normalised current/retired spelling maps to exactly one lane, vendor present in VENDORS, runtime in {claude, codex}, exactly one scarce lane, fallback fields only on a lane whose runtime is claude. The test compares records against each other and against the spec's shape; it does not repeat concrete name literals.

One `LEGACY` map in model-lanes.mjs holds every old persisted spelling beside its new one; readers normalise through it, writers emit only the new spelling. Routing setting values: `claude-only` -> `main-only`, `default` -> `default`, `prefer-astra` -> `prefer-cross`; state file `.claude/astra-share.json` -> `.claude/lane-routing.json`, the old file read when the new one is absent and never rewritten in place. All compatibility data lives in this map so no consumer embeds a retired name.

`reviewIdentityProblem(reviewer, commit)` resolves the reviewer and each parsed author/reviewer trailer through `resolveModel` and returns a reason string or null. The existing trailer parser keeps parsing complete `Name <addr>` entries (comma/semicolon separated) before resolution, with only the already-supported suffix grammar ('(1M context)', '[1m]'); substring matches and model-like addresses are not accepted. The adversarial fixtures in model-guard-core.test.mjs are retained (U23).

Cross-vendor rule: the reviewer lane's `vendor` must differ from every relevant author lane's `vendor`; `cross` is a lane key, not a promise that this lane may review everyone. Fallback chains are role lists in data: `REVIEW_CHAINS = { crossUnavailable: ['main'], scarceUnavailable: ['main'] }` (names refined by the author, roles only). Fail closed: an unresolved author or an empty eligible set is a refusal with reason, never a same-vendor fallback; when the authors jointly cover every registered vendor the script reports a review conflict instead of dropping an author.

cross-review.mjs collects authors over the reviewed range and recorded contributions exactly as review-astra does today (no scope change), then selects the first enabled eligible reviewer from REVIEW_CHAINS order, optionally forced with `--reviewer <role>`; it invokes that lane through its runtime (claude or codex), so main reviewing cross-authored work runs through the same script. This is the only behavioural addition beyond renaming and is required by the spec sentence 'review by a lane of another vendor than the author'.

Renames, each with its -core, -cli.test, -core.test, -plan/-contribution/-session test siblings: fable-switch-core.mjs identity part -> model-lanes.mjs, switch part -> lane-switch-core.mjs; fable-switch.mjs -> lane-switch.mjs (`--lane <role> --on|--off|--status`); astra-share(-core) -> lane-routing(-core); review-astra(-core) -> cross-review(-core); ask-astra(-core) -> ask-lane(-core) with `--lane <role>` replacing `--model fable|astra`; author-astra.mjs + author-fable.mjs -> author-delegate.mjs `--lane <role>` with author-astra-core.mjs becoming author-delegate-core.mjs and author-fable-core's 55 lines folded in behind the runtime switch, all lane-specific test cases kept. DECIDED: no compatibility wrappers, no CLI aliases; old filenames are deleted on the same branch (both halves agree; a wrapper under an old name would itself violate the filename rule).

DECIDED: `codex` and `claude` are the spec-mandated runtime values, not vendor or model names, so runtime-specific functions keep their runtime word where they live today (`runCodex`, `codexArgs`, `authoringCodexArgs`, `codexTokens`, `parseCodexTranscript`, `listCodexRollouts`, `CODEX_BIN`, `CODEX_HOME`); only `MEASURE_CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR` -> `MEASURE_RUNTIME_SESSIONS_DIR` is renamed because it is this project's own env name (U16). REJECTED B29/B35/B59: a new `runtime-adapters.mjs` with neutral adapter names is a new abstraction under the freeze. Dispatch is one `switch (lane.runtime)` in author-delegate-core; the model id passed to the runtime is `lane(role).modelId` or the main fallback, no caller-supplied raw override. Refusal classification, cancellation, cleanup, session attribution, token accounting and fallback triggers are untouched, and the existing codex protocol tests keep their captured fixtures.

Function renames with an explicit lane argument instead of a hidden fixed lane: recordAstraRun -> recordLaneRun(role, ...), afterAstraRun -> afterLaneRun(role, ...), astraAuthored -> authoredByLane(role, ...), kindsToAstra -> kindsToLane(role); fableIsOn -> laneIsOn(role), fableRefusalReason -> laneRefusalReason(role), fableStateAtCommit -> laneStateAtCommit(role, sha), fableAuthoringOutcome -> laneAuthoringOutcome(role), currentFableState -> currentLaneState(role).
FABLE_ESCALATION_ROUNDS -> SCARCE_ESCALATION_ROUNDS in the core, its .d.mts and the one src consumer; src/config/fableEscalationDoc.test.ts is renamed to scarceEscalationDoc.test.ts.

Env renames: ASTRA_SHARE_FILE -> LANE_ROUTING_FILE, FABLE_SWITCH_FILE -> LANE_SWITCH_FILE, FABLE_SWITCH_SET_BY -> LANE_SWITCH_SET_BY, REVIEW_ASTRA_STATE_DIR -> CROSS_REVIEW_STATE_DIR, MEASURE_CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR -> MEASURE_RUNTIME_SESSIONS_DIR; CODEX_HOME stays (external Codex CLI contract). DECIDED: new names only. REJECTED B37 (read legacy env aliases, accept equivalent duals, error on conflicts): these variables are set by scripts in the same tree and by the daemon, which is restarted after landing (U32); dual-reading is migration machinery the freeze excludes.

DECIDED per-lane switch format: `.claude/lane-switch.json` = `{ lanes: { <role>: { state, reason, setBy, changedAt } } }` in the MAIN checkout through the existing authoritative-path mechanism; absent roles take the defaults main=on, cross=on, scarce=off, so the scarce lane still needs an explicit `--on` and nothing is switched off by accident. The legacy `.claude/fable-switch.json` is read as the scarce entry when the new file is absent and left on disk as the recoverable copy; the new file is written only on the first `lane-switch --lane ... --on/--off`. REJECTED B43 (versioned, locked, atomic, repeatable migration): the state is one small JSON written by one operator command, and the freeze forbids new guards and locks. `laneStateAtCommit(role, sha)` reads the legacy path and schema when the queried revision predates the rename. Reachability probes never flip a switch. Operationally: no authoring or review process runs while the owner flips state, and losing the scarce gate is a release blocker checked by the switch tests.

Persisted route ids and outcomes through the LEGACY map: astra-authored and sol-authored -> cross-authored; astra-only and sol-only -> cross-only; astra-unavailable and sol-unavailable -> lane-unavailable with a `lane` field. Before mapping, each remaining I10 token is classified in the tree: `sole` is an English word, `sol-work`, `bulk-sol`, `sol-turn`, `astra-turn`, `first-opus`, `last-fable` and the `hoa-*`/`review-astra-cli-` temp prefixes are checked for whether they are persisted or purely in-process before they get a legacy entry or a plain rename.

Trailers keep real model names: `trailerFor(role, {fallback})` returns `<trailerName> <vendor trailerAddress>` and, when the main lane ran on its fallback, the fallback name instead, so the trailer names the model that actually worked. model-trailer-gate verifies landed trailers through `resolveModel`, so GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra trailers keep passing.

Ledgers are never rewritten; readers normalise `model`, `claimedModel`, `authoredBy` through `resolveModel` in memory and the existing claim-versus-evidence checks keep running on the resolved lane. REJECTED B50/B51 (new `lane` field and schema version in new records): the freeze forbids new ledger fields, and the role is derivable from the stored model name through the registry at read time. Tests assert that old records and trailers resolve byte-for-byte unchanged and that a record written today still resolves after the cross lane's modelId is edited in a synthetic registry.

Reachability stays the existing manual probe recorded by the owner (spec: the new id is proven on this machine before the lane counts as reachable); no unit test claims gpt-6.1-sol answers. REJECTED B62 (probe evidence bound to role, model id, runtime and install path with invalidation): that is a new ledger, and the amendment already makes the global probe a human gate.

Behaviour kept, names generalised: authorship-check keeps model claims, transcript evidence and observed author separate; measure-point-cost dispatches transcript and token parsing on `lane.runtime` and leaves historical cost records as stored. The codex fixture files under scripts/fixtures/point-cost/ keep their names and bytes.

Tests import lane data directly (`lane('cross').trailerName`, `trailerFor('main')`, `lane('main').retired[0]`) across ALL measured test files, not only the spec's 114/28 count which the inventory I8 already exceeds. REJECTED B66's shared `test-support/lane-fixtures.mjs`: a module whose job is to re-export the registry is a second source. Adversarial model-guard cases are composed from registry names plus synthetic unknowns (Haiku, Nano, malformed punctuation) built inline; cross-review tests run the three cross names pairwise against self-review, reject different-role/same-vendor reviewers, and pass a synthetic registry with a third vendor through the `registry` argument (U6); compatibility readers are tested legacy-only, new-only, malformed and partially migrated (no dual-conflict cases, per U17).

DECIDED: the hygiene check 'no consumer names a concrete model' is a unit test inside model-lanes.test.mjs, not a separate checker script or guard (freeze). It lists tracked files under scripts/ (names and contents, comments included) and the operational docs of U28, excludes model-lanes.mjs itself, scripts/fixtures/ and the test's own file, and fails on any token derived from the registry (current and retired names and ids, vendor tokens, legacy map keys) plus one pattern built from the registry's family words followed by a version digit, so a freshly hard-coded 'GPT-7 Astra' is caught. REJECTED B77's reviewed-path manifest with baseline hashes and B73's separate maintained checker: the exclusion list is three fixed path prefixes, and growth of it is reviewed like any test change. The test is self-exercised with a synthetic violating file in a temp dir.

DECIDED on comments: current-state comments in touched scripts are rewritten to roles. src/ historical attribution comments (the 27 I12 lines in balance.ts, PlaceScene.tsx, layout.ts, appearance.ts etc.) and en.ts game prose are NOT touched: they are provenance records like trailers, src/ is not a consumer of lane data, and the hygiene test does not scan src/. REJECTED B80 (replace them with point/artifact references): it rewrites history for no functional gain. Historical docs (tasks-archive, blind-*, four-eyes/<point>-*, analysis_de, communication-review-659, point-cost-*, backlog entries, rule-corpus-audit), ledgers and scripts/fixtures/ are records outside the boundary; ordinary test inputs are generated from lane data (U24).

§6 lines 72-83 rewritten to roles only: main chain, cross-vendor reviewer, scarce lane; the sentence 'GPT-6 Astra authors difficult/complex/error-prone/HIGH points' and the per-model authoring assignments are deleted; `scripts/review-astra.mjs` and `scripts/fable-switch.mjs --status` references become cross-review.mjs and `lane-switch.mjs --lane scarce --status`. Text says that routing default authors on main, which matches live practice since 26.09.

Besides static imports, every dynamic reference follows: subprocess paths (`node scripts/...`), package.json commands, test discovery patterns, help output, temp-file prefixes (`hoa-fable-switch-`, `hoa-astra-share-`, `review-astra-cli-`), error codes and generated command references; `scripts/module-link-check.mjs` and `git-tracked.test.mjs` are rerun against the final tree.

Order on one branch: (1) model-lanes.mjs with the GPT-6.1 cross lane, VENDORS, LEGACY map and its test; (2) guards, trailer gate, mechanism-review and authorship readers consume it, old constants become re-exports for the moment; (3) the renames of U13 and function renames of U15 in one commit per script family with their tests; (4) switch and routing state readers; (5) tests, comments, docs, CLAUDE.md, memory; (6) delete transitional re-exports and old filenames, then enable the hygiene test. The old exports are never removed before all consumers compile, so no intermediate commit runs a guard without identity resolution.

A running daemon or batch on main keeps invoking the old script names from its loaded code until restarted; landing ends with a runbook step that the owner restarts the daemon after merge and before the next point starts.

Size: on the order of 240 touched files and one large rename; conflicts with concurrent main work are expected, so the branch is rebased immediately before landing and landed in one go, not left open across other points.

Both blind halves and this union are filed unchanged under docs/four-eyes/1393-*; the implementation is reviewed by an eligible lane of the other vendor from the author, through the renamed cross-review.mjs once it runs, and the review is void if substantive reviewed code changes afterwards. This design merge is not that review.

Completion means: unit suite, build, lint green; hygiene test green; compatibility tests green; a smoke run of author-delegate --lane cross and cross-review against the global Codex install. The inventory gets a closing before/after section listing what still matches the broad search pattern and why (runtime words, fixtures, history, src comments, en.ts prose) instead of claiming zero.

Because the registry now governs both what may execute and whose trailer is trusted, any later edit to LANES, VENDORS or LEGACY is treated as guard-level change: cross-vendor reviewed and covered by the invariant test of U8 so an accidental alias cannot merge two lanes.
1393 lands before point 1347 per the work order; 1347 resumes only after the daemon restart (U33) and memory update (U30) so it never runs against half-migrated switch or routing state.
